summary: Fan out read-only investigators across Harbor seams to find SDK/headless-embedding friction, adversarially verify blockers/majors
logs: Survey complete: 10/10 seams reported; 62 raw findings.

seams.seam: Run loop + task execution semantics (cmd/harbor/cmd_dev_runloop.go, cmd_dev_executor.go, cmd_dev_catalog_view.go, dev_enricher.go, internal/tasks, internal/runtime/steering, harbortest/devstack)
seams.summary: The step-loop core is genuinely clean: steering.NewRunLoop (internal/runtime/steering/runloop.go:182) exports the inbox-draining, pause/resume routing, control projection, trajectory-append, and ToolExecutor-dispatch semantics behind a proper options constructor, and internal/tasks exports the full registry/FSM. Everything ABOVE the loop, however, is production semantics living in package main: the only production steering.ToolExecutor (D-026 heavy-content projection, CallParallel aggregation, SpawnTask/AwaitTask driving), the task-FSM bridge with its error-code taxonomy and the Phase-106 answer envelope, the entire RunContext population layer (memory/skills projection, skill-keyword extraction, input-artifact resolution), and the bus-emission closures (planner telemetry Emit, llm.completion.chunk envelopes). A headless consumer building on steering.RunLoop + tasks.TaskRegistry would have to reimplement roughly 1,000 lines of cmd code, and the D-026 LLM-edge guard (internal/llm/safety.go:99) guarantees their first naive attempt fails loudly on any heavy tool result. Notably, cmd_dev_runloop.go and cmd_dev_executor.go contain zero CLI-specific plumbing — they import only internal/ packages and take plain config values — so promotion to internal/runtime/runloop (or similar) is essentially a mechanical move-and-export; planner.BuildArtifactManifest (internal/planner/artifact_manifest.go) already demonstrates the promotion pattern applied to exactly one of these helpers. Meanwhile the D-094 devstack mirror has materially diverged from cmd (CallTool-only executor with no D-026 promotion, empty MarkComplete result, no streaming/telemetry wiring), so the public test kit now validates weaker semantics than production ships.

frictions.why: This is the Phase 83f / D-149 failure class verbatim: steering.ToolExecutor is an exported seam whose only production filler is cmd/harbor. A headless consumer wiring steering.NewRunLoop with their own executor cannot get correct multi-step tool execution: the D-026 invariant is enforced runtime-wide (ErrContextLeak), but the only implementation of the discipline — including the artifact-promotion path, the provenance stamping the Console/manifest layers expect ('source':'tool', 'created_at'), and the preview heuristics hardened against the 1.5MB-tool-result failure — is unexported in package main. frictions.recommendation: Promote devToolExecutor to an exported constructor in internal/runtime (e.g. internal/runtime/dispatch.NewToolExecutor(catalog, artifactStore, taskRegistry, opts...)), keeping cmd/harbor as a thin caller. The struct already has zero CLI dependencies (catalog + store + registry + logger + two ints). At minimum, export projectForLLM/heavyTruncationSummary as a reusable D-026 projection helper next to the threshold it pairs with — the invariant that punishes its absence is already in internal/llm.

verdict.reason: Every cited line verifies. devToolExecutor (cmd/harbor/cmd_dev_executor.go:61, package main, unexported) is the only complete steering.ToolExecutor in the module; the only other implementation, harbortest/devstack's devStackToolExecutor (devstack.go:2105), is also unexported, hardwired (no injection option in AssembleOpts), and explicitly degraded — its own comment admits it skips D-026 promotion and it handles CallTool only, returning ErrDecisionShapeUnsupported for CallParallel/SpawnTask/AwaitTask. No exported constructor or projection helper exists anywhere (no NewToolExecutor; internal/llm/materialize.go helpers are all unexported and handle only DataURLs). The failure mechanism is real: internal/llm/safety.go's findContextLeak checks message text (not just DataURLs), and auto-materialization rescues only DataURLs, so a hand-rolled executor without the projectForLLM discipline deterministically trips ErrContextLeak on the first heavy tool result. frictions.why: Beyond the known headline (no driver in internal/), the semantics the driver encodes are an undocumented contract a headless consumer must reverse-engineer: the exact Finish.Reason→TaskError.Code mapping, the cancelled-vs-failed decision (D-098), and especially the answer envelope — which the executor's AwaitTask/retain-turn SpawnTask path parses by shape. A consumer who drives their own loop and marks tasks complete with a different TaskResult.Value shape silently breaks spawn/await joins, harbortest assertions, and any Protocol projector reading result_inline. None of these shapes (envelope struct, code constants) exist as exported types; they are string literals and ad-hoc maps in package main.
frictions.recommendation: Define the answer envelope as an exported type (e.g. tasks.AnswerEnvelope or planner.RunOutcome) with Marshal/Unmarshal helpers in internal/tasks or internal/planner, plus exported constants for the terminal error codes ('runloop_error', 'cancelled', 'runtime_fetch_error'). Then make both cmd files and devstack consume them. This is the smallest change that makes a hand-rolled driver wire-compatible; full driver promotion (finding on the known headline) subsumes it later.

verdict.reason: Core claim verified: the Finish.Reason→TaskError.Code mapping, the error-code strings ('runloop_error', 'cancelled', 'runtime_fetch_error'), and the {answer, finish_reason, tool_calls_seen} envelope exist only as string literals and ad-hoc maps in package main (cmd/harbor) plus a hand-copied mirror in harbortest/devstack — no exported type, constants, or Marshal/Unmarshal helpers anywhere in internal/. Bonus evidence FOR the finding: devstack has ALREADY drifted — its FinishGoal path calls MarkComplete with an empty tasks.TaskResult{} (never gained the Phase-106 envelope), a live D-094 helper-tracks-production violation proving the lack of a shared type causes real divergence. And the Console Playground's answer-envelope.ts strictly requires a string "answer" key, so a hand-rolled headless driver with a different Value shape does blank the Playground answer. However, three of the finding's impact claims are overstated or false: (1) "D-098 rationale lives only in this comment block" is false — docs/decisions.md:1893 carries a full D-098 entry with the complete exit-shape mapping and a dedicated Cancellation-handling section; (2) "undocumented contract a headless consumer must reverse-engineer" is overstated — the envelope shape is documented in godoc on tasks.TaskResult (internal/tasks/tasks.go:267-281) with an explicit "Consumers MAY rely on this shape" + additive-evolution promise, precisely where a headless consumer would look; (3) "silently breaks spawn/await joins" is wrong — taskOutcomeObservation (cmd_dev_executor.go:423-443) is shape-tolerant (generic json.Unmarshal into any, raw-string fallback), so joins survive any Value shape; only the Console answer rendering and semantic richness degrade. "Breaks harbortest assertions" is also wrong in detail (harbortest neither produces nor asserts the envelope). With the breakage claims corrected, what remains is "documented-in-prose but not codified; consumer must hand-copy literals" — real SDK friction (and the lens forbids refuting on that basis), but materially less severe than presented, and the finding itself concedes the headline driver-promotion finding subsumes it. Downgrade from major to minor.

Minor framing caveat: Assemble takes *testing.T and AssembleOpts names internal/ types, so genuinely external modules can't practically use it — but the verification lens defines headless consumer as in-module code, for which the finding holds exactly as stated; if anything the caveat reveals additional friction (the 'operator-importable from outside the module' billing in CLAUDE.md §3 is itself partly broken). Severity 'major' is calibrated: not a blocker (production behaves correctly; the harm is the official kit validating weaker semantics — the repo's own §17.6 F1 divergence class), but well above minor given five independent capability gaps plus a violated same-PR mirror contract.

seams.summary: The core of the seam is genuinely clean: llm.Open mandatorily wraps every driver in the safety client, so heavy-content materialization, the ErrContextLeak edge guard, and the token-budget guard are active for ANY headless caller by construction (internal/llm/registry.go:452, :421-425), and the memory Summarizer (internal/llm/summarizer/summarizer.go:132) and PostureProvider (internal/llm/posture.go:110) are exported, programmatic constructors. The friction is in the outer wrapper chain: corrections, structured-output downgrade, retry-with-feedback, governance, and the per-provider default-OutputMode resolver are seated ONLY by blank imports in cmd/harbor/main.go:51-68, and llm.Open silently skips any unseated wrapper (`if wrap != nil`), so a headless consumer — including one following devstack's own documented import recipe — gets safety(driver) instead of the documented production chain governance(retry(downgrade(corrections(safety(driver))))), with no error or warning. Worse, governance ENFORCEMENT (cost ceilings, rate limits, MaxTokens — RFC §6.15) is wired nowhere in production: governance.SetFactory is called only in a test, so even the dev binary only projects posture; configuring identity_tiers enforces nothing on any path. Finally, the config.LLMConfig → llm.ConfigSnapshot mapping is hand-rolled and duplicated in cmd_dev.go and devstack.go with private helpers — the exact duplication that already produced the 83l/D-155 silently-dropped-fields production bug — and there is no exported constructor a headless consumer could use instead.

frictions.why: A headless in-module consumer who calls llm.Open after importing only internal/llm gets a chain missing per-provider corrections (NIM reordering, Anthropic envelope, usage backfill), structured-output downgrade, validator retry, the governance hook, and per-provider OutputMode defaults — silently. frictions.recommendation: Smallest change: in llm.Open, when a Disable* flag is false and the corresponding hook is nil, fail loudly (or at minimum slog.Warn + emit a bus event naming the missing blank import). verdict.reason: Every cited line checks out, and the strongest refutation avenue (an importable assembly alternative) actively confirms the finding instead of refuting it. (3) The OutputMode-resolver claim holds: applyDefaults (registry.go:529-554) reads the corrections-registered resolver; nil resolver → profiles stay OutputModeUnset and the comment itself says 'the downgrade chain skips them'. (4) No exported alternative exists: a repo-wide grep shows the only non-test importers of internal/llm/corrections, internal/llm/output, internal/llm/retry are cmd/harbor/main.go and two integration tests that hand-roll the blank-import block themselves (test/integration/wave7b_test.go:73-77 must blank-import all four packages to reproduce the production chain — direct proof there is no single importable assembly leaf). (5) Decisive additional evidence: harbortest/devstack — the repo's own canonical importable assembly helper, whose godoc claims it 'MUST track the production boot stack in cmd/harbor/cmd_dev.go::bootDevStack field-for-field' — calls llm.Open at devstack.go:602 but does NOT blank-import corrections, output, or retry. The in-repo helper itself exhibits the exact failure mode the finding describes, and asymmetrically, which is arguably worse than all-or-nothing. seams.summary: The registration and reliability layers of this seam are genuinely SDK-clean: tools.NewCatalog, inproc.RegisterFunc, the RunWithPolicy/RunWithPolicyHooked reliability shell, http.LoadManifest/RegisterManifest, mcp.New, a2a.New, builtin.RegisterWith, the Phase 64a catalog.Builder (approval+OAuth wrapping incl. exported WrapWithApproval/WrapWithOAuth), and auth.NewProvider/InitiateFlow/CompleteFlow are all exported, programmatically constructible, and not config-locked. The friction concentrates one layer up, at dispatch and assembly: the only full implementation of steering.ToolExecutor (CallTool + CallParallel + SpawnTask/AwaitTask + D-026 heavy-result artifact promotion) is cmd-local package-main code with a deliberately degraded devstack mirror, so a headless consumer cannot execute parallel/spawn decisions or get heavy-content discipline without rewriting ~660 lines. Provider attach lifecycles (MCP config→Connect→Discover→Register, incl. policy projection) live only in cmd + a diverged devstack copy, and the HTTP-manifest / A2A config knobs are validated but wired nowhere at all. Approval resolution headless works but forces an internal/protocol/auth scope stamp on ctx, and the OAuth completion leg (CompleteFlow) has zero production callers — the "Harbor Protocol callback handler" the godocs reference does not exist. Net: a headless consumer can register and invoke tools with the full reliability shell today, but must hand-roll the decision dispatcher, the catalog→planner view adapter, every provider-attach loop, the OAuth callback endpoint, and the KEK/sealer/tokenstore assembly.

seams.summary: The core primitives are genuinely SDK-shaped: pauseresume.New with functional options (WithBus, WithCheckpointStore, WithHandleRegistry — coordinator.go:71-135), the full Coordinator interface including List with a caller-set AdminScoped flag that deliberately keeps Protocol auth out (pauseresume.go:200-250, 254-273 / D-079), and a fully exported steering surface (NewRegistry, Registry.Lookup, Inbox.Enqueue with steering-local Scope vocabulary, NewRunLoop with options) — so a headless consumer can receive a pause (bus pause.requested carries the Token — events.go:40-46), enqueue all nine controls, and resume, entirely from Go. The friction is concentrated one layer up, in how pauses are actually driven: the only in-process HITL resolution helper demands Protocol auth scopes on ctx (gate.go:353-355); an approval-gated tool dispatched by a real planner deadlocks the RunLoop's drain-at-step-boundary design, so the D-097 steering→gate bridge can never fire for the canonical HITL shape and no in-tree code (cmd, devstack, or test) demonstrates a working choreography for it; durable pauses (WithCheckpointStore) have zero production consumers and the RunLoop checkpoints a nil trajectory; the OAuth pause's resume half (CompleteFlow) is wired nowhere; and no pause GC/expiry exists despite DecisionTimeout being defined. Net: simple planner-RequestPause + steering-resume is cleanly reachable headless; HITL-on-tool-call, durable-restartable pause, and OAuth-pause completion all require the consumer to invent choreography that does not exist even on the dev-binary path.

seams.seam: Configuration duality, repo-wide: programmatic construction paths vs config-file-only knobs across internal/config and every subsystem factory
seams.summary: The per-subsystem story is mostly healthy: state, artifacts, events, sessions, audit, tasks, and the tool catalog accept config sub-structs directly in exported factories (state.Open(cfg.State), sessions.New(store, cfg.Sessions, bus), catalog.New(entries, deps)), so a headless in-module consumer can construct them with or without a YAML file. The friction concentrates one layer up: the five subsystems that decouple via snapshot/boundary types (llm, memory, skills, planner, governance) keep the config→snapshot projection as unexported helpers in package main, duplicated in harbortest/devstack — and that duplication has already produced one shipped silent-field-drop bug (D-155) and one live drift bug today (devstack's plannerConfigFromConfig drops ExtraGuidance/ReasoningReplay/MaxToolExamplesPerTool/ParallelToolCalls). There is no reusable *config.Config→stack fan-out outside bootDevStack (package main) and devstack.Assemble (which requires *testing.T), so config-without-binary means re-implementing ~700 lines of assembly. Two config blocks are outright dead: tools.http_manifests is validated but consumed by nothing anywhere, and governance.identity_tiers drives only a read-only posture view while its documented enforcement (SetFactory + the cost/rate/max-tokens enforcers) has zero production call sites. Finally, the run-loop-projected planner knobs (skills_context_max, planning_hints, spawn depth, granted_scopes), the loader-only defaults, and the unconditional JWT-identity validation make the YAML surface systematically richer than — and occasionally contradictory to — the programmatic surface, with no recipe documenting the headless path in either direction.

seams.seam: External-module surface: harbortest/ (+ devstack), examples/, docs/recipes/, README, and the internal/ import boundary
seams.summary: For a genuinely EXTERNAL Go module, Harbor's entire importable surface is harbortest/ and harbortest/devstack/ — every runtime package lives under internal/. An empirical probe (temp module github.com/example/probe with a replace directive) confirms: importing internal/tools fails with "use of internal package ... not allowed", while harbortest-only code builds. Within harbortest, only the zero-Deps RunOnce + AssertNoLeaks + EventLog reads actually work externally; AssertSequence, the whole FaultInjector surface, and every Deps field are type-poisoned by internal types the caller can neither name nor construct, and an external Agent cannot emit events or read identity at all, making the captured EventLog structurally empty. Worse, the product's own golden path is broken: harbor scaffold generates an external module (module github.com/example/<name>) whose agent.go imports internal/tools, internal/tools/builtin, and internal/tools/drivers/inproc the moment harbor.yaml declares any tool — code that can never compile — and the only build-checking smoke (phase-67.sh) exercises only the no-tools template. devstack, the de-facto production assembly, is importable but unusable externally (internal *config.Config parameter, mandatory blank-imports of internal driver packages, *testing.T-flavoured entry with the error-returning core unexported). The RFC §1 "ships as a Go module" claim is therefore true only for in-module consumers today; making it true externally requires promoting (or facading) roughly: identity, events, config-or-options, tools (+inproc/builtin), llm, the store ifaces+factories+driver registration paths, planner/tasks/steering, and a non-testing assembly entry.
